subject: DPA Retention & Erasure: proposed tiered sunset + onshore backup carveout
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acme-med.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acme-med.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on retention carveouts & onshore backup in DPA (Acme)

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft DPA. Our legal team flagged two sticking points we need to resolve before we can sign: 1) the retention/erase timeline language (Section 4.2 in the draft) is written as a single-window erase for production + backups, which is a hard compliance risk for us in EEA clinical trials, and 2) the backup/onshore copy carveout — we need explicit onshore backup handling and proof of erasure for onshore snapshots when a customer requests deletion.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood accept a tiered sunset where primary data is erased within X days but backups are subject to a defined escrow/onshore retention with a certified erase trigger?
- Can you provide a short playbook for how you would demonstrate erasure from onshore backups (logs/artifacts/certificates) and an SLA for evidence delivery?

I attached our redlines (acme_supplement_comments.docx) — mostly small edits and a suggested clause for certification.

We can do a quick sync if helpful; prefer Wed (PST morning) if either of you are available.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Stone
Procurement Manager — Acme Medical
[Attachment: acme_supplement_comments.docx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@acme-med.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention carveouts & onshore backup in DPA (Acme)

Emma — thanks for the redlines and for outlining the operational ask. Appreciate the specificity.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can propose a tiered sunset that separates primary production erasure from backups, with defined triggers for backup paraphernalia (snapshots/replicas).
- We can provide a certified erasure packet for onshore backups (logs, wipe job IDs, storage-layer object deletion events) within the time window you require — subject to a maximum document delivery SLA (we suggest 10 business days).

What we propose (quick summary):
1) Tiered retention model (proposed language attached):
   - Primary user data: permanent deletion within 30 days of customer request (configurable per account).
   - Warm-tier snapshots: retained for up to 90 days and then rotated; eligible for expedited purge on verified legal request if customer opts into an onshore purge addendum.
   - Cold backups/archives: retained for up to 12 months unless customer purchases immediate erase option.

2) Onshore backup carveout:
   - Onshore backups will be stored in customer-designated region(s) when requested; Redwood will run targeted wipe jobs against onshore storage and provide signed certificates of deletion for affected objects.

3) Evidence playbook & SLA:
   - Erasure packet: wipe job ID, timestamped storage events, operator runbook excerpt, and audit log snippet (redacted where necessary).
   - Delivery SLA: default 10 business days; expedited 3 business days available as a premium compliance option.

Next steps: we attached a brief proposal PDF (redwood-tiered-retention-proposal.pdf) with suggested DPA language you can mark up. If this aligns, happy to schedule a 30-min call Wed 10:00 PST to walk through the exact redlines.

Thanks — looping in Karthik for infra/backup mechanics.

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-tiered-retention-proposal.pdf]

Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention carveouts & onshore backup in DPA (Acme)

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the pragmatic framing. A couple of follow-ups from legal and security: 

1) Erasure packet contents — legal wants explicit statement that the packet includes chain-of-custody metadata (operator ID, job hash) and that Redwood will keep proof of erase for X months (they've asked for 24 months). Is that feasible?
2) Warm-tier expedited purge — legal asked whether purge can be executed across cross-region replicas within the expedited SLA (i.e., if data was geo-replicated for availability). They want to be sure an expedited purge won't leave stale copies outside the onshore region.

We've flagged a few suggested edits inline in the PDF; attaching a version with short comments. If you can confirm by EOD tomorrow we can aim to move to signatures next week.

Emma

Subject: Re: Questions on retention carveouts & onshore backup in DPA (Acme)

Emma — quick status and concrete answers to your follow-ups below. We reviewed with infra and legal (Olga).

1) Chain-of-custody and retention of proof: we can include operator ID and wipe job hash in the erasure packet. Redwood will retain signed erasure evidence records for 24 months as requested and provide them on request; we will include a paragraph in the DPA specifying this retention period for proof-of-erasure artifacts.

2) Cross-region replicas: our standard behavior for expedited purge is to target all replicas associated with the object across regions where Redwood has control. For geo-replicated copies that are held by a third-party (e.g., a cloud vendor outside the control plane), we will document the scope and provide a fallback remediation plan (certified replication sweep + follow-up cert). If you require hard jurisdictional guarantees (no copies outside specified region under any condition), that becomes an onshore-only hosting requirement and we can provide an optional addendum for regional-only storage with a pricing impact.

3) SLA for evidence delivery: default 10 business days; expedited 3 business days at premium. We will accept contract language that allows Redwood to redact operator personal data in the erasure packet (we will include operator ID and job hash, but full operator names will be redacted for privacy).

4) Suggested DPA insertion: we propose the following short clause to add as an appendix: "Upon verified customer erasure request, Redwood will initiate targeted wipe jobs against all customer-designated primary and onshore backup objects and provide a signed erasure packet within the agreed SLA. Proof-of-erasure records will be retained by Redwood for 24 months." (legal to refine wording).

Next steps: Olga will circulate a clean DPA appendix with the agreed retention-of-evidence and cross-region carveouts for a final review. If that looks good we can prepare an amendment for signatures by next week.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if you want to walk through the technical sweep plan.

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
